parsed_response.reasoning: The string[] header comparison issue is real: Next.js req.headers values can be string|string[], so a duplicated webhook header (array) compared with !== against the string secret always yields a spurious 403. However, the primary bypass claim is partly contradicted by the diff: the handler first checks APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, which constants.ts defines as requiring CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET to be set, so both-undefined comparison cannot reach the secret check (the first 403 fires). Only if the secret is set to an empty string (as in .env.example default "") would the empty-vs-empty comparison pass without real auth. The remaining verifiable mechanism (header type mismatch and empty-string secret acceptance) is a genuine defect in newly added code, so this is a bug, though weaker than stated.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret check compares `req.headers[...]` directly to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. In Next.js, `req.headers[name]` can be `string | string[] | undefined`; if the header is duplicated it may be a `string[]`, which will never equal the env string and will cause an unintended 403 (“spurious 403s”). The claimed bypass when both header and secret are undefined is not verifiable here because the handler first blocks unless `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is truthy, and that constant is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so the code path with an undefined secret is gated off.
